newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian football veteran ruckman Justin Madden was asked to play one last game by Carlton coach David Parkin on Tuesday in front of the changeroom lockers at Optus Oval. After the 15 minute conversation Madden said that his body was gone. Page 2.

Dr Ken Fitch said yesterday that Australia needed to lift its game and to attack the problem more seriously, otherwise drugs would be a factor at the Sydney Olympics. Fitch is Australia's representative on the International Olympic Committee's Medical Comission. Page 20.

Young Australian tennis player Luke Smith, 20, ranked No.620 will play in the first ATP tour of the Washington Classic this week after winning a wild card. Former Davis Cup player John Fitzgerald rang Pat Rafter yesterday and asked him to befriend Smith on his arrival in America. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Swimmer Susan O'Neill will take to the blocks in Melbourne today marking the start of the Australian shortcourse swimming championships. O'Neill is one of the three highest-paid sportswomen in Australia alongside runner Cathy Freeman and golfer Karrie Web. Page 47.

There is speculation the Australian Rugby League plan to sell mergers to fans will be impossible if some clubs are allowed to stand alone. Chief executives of Sydney clubs are supporting the old rugby league adage "one in, all in". Page 48.

Former Australian cricket player Ross Edwards, now a BSkyB executive responsible for marketing cricket telecasts in England, has presented a plan for a Test world championship to the International Cricket Council. Edward's plan is for a competition to runover four years, and have six teams in three divisions. Page 48.
THE AGE

In the quarter-final of the Women's amateur golf championships at Victoria Golf Club yesterday, Queensland's top junior Tamara Johns won over Victorian veteran Carolyn Carlos 2 and 1. In the qualifying rounds Carlos qualified first with a par round of 74, Johns qualified ninth. Page B6.

Basketball's Melbourne Tigers assistant coach Alan Westover questioned Mark Bradtke yesterday on rumours that he is set to leave the club at the end of the year. Bradtke answered saying the rumours were merely someone trying to stir the pot. He becomes a free agent at the end of the season. Page B6.

Essendon coach Kevin Sheedy was given unconditional support to coach the club next season by president Graeme McMahon last night amidst more speculation that Sheedy is under pressure to retain his position. McMahon gave Sheedy a declaration of confidence11 days ago at a club lunch. Sheedy's position was questioned last week following his criticism of manager Noel Judkins. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Key Carlton player Fraser Brown's career may be in jeopardy after being ruled out for the rest of the season following an operation today to repair an injured hamstring. Blues Coach David Parkin said he can't power up his legs to make himself run. Page 8.

Australian Socceroo player Ernie Tapai is about to sign a two-year contract worth almost $A200,000 to play for Perth Glory in this summer's Ericsson Cup. Tapai played for the Collingwood Warriors last season. Page 79.

Former Australian cricket batsman Dean Jones said yesterday that he wanted to become a national selector. Jones, who has been out of the Australian team over the past three years, said he wanted to be a decision-maker rather than someone who always waited for decisions to be made. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
A bid of $4 million to buy the Auckland Warriors was made to the Auckland Rugby League last night. The bid was made by a syndicate headed by former Manly and New Zealand coach Graham Lowe. Page 88.

Leading Waratah official Ron Meagher said last night that it will be the board of the New South Wales Rugby Union and not the clubs who will decide which teams will take part in rugby union's AAMI cup competition. The statement comes after a meeting which called for the Canberra Kookaburras to be one of the two clubs dropped from the competition next year. Page 86.

Australian golfer Greg Norman, better known as the Great White Shark, is an all-action, fearless hero who has complied a list of daring things he still wants to do. Norman, 42, still wants to cruise down the Amazon, mountain climb and fly in a space shuttle all before he dies. Page 82.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
